summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with septic shock secondary to bacterial pneumonia and coffee-ground emesis. He was started on broad-spectrum antibiotics, including Linezolid and Meropenem, but developed an allergic reaction to cefepime, which was substituted with aztreonam and metronidazole. An EGD revealed mild esophagitis and gastritis without active bleeding, and he responded well to treatment with omeprazole. His acute kidney injury resolved with hydration, and his constipation improved with a bowel regimen. The right hip wound showed no signs of re-infection, and he remained non-weight-bearing as instructed. He completed a 7-day course of IV antibiotics and was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned for allergy testing and primary care.
